sources.entry: TensorFlow - Open-source machine learning framework by Google.

summary.name: TensorFlow
summary.one_liner: TensorFlow is an open-source, end-to-end machine learning platform for building and deploying ML models across many environments.
use_cases: Deploying ML models to mobile and edge devices
Running models in the browser with JavaScript
Preprocessing data for ML input pipelines
summary.what_it_does: The page presents TensorFlow as an open-source platform for creating ML models that can run in any environment. It shows a short Python example using tf.keras to train a simple classifier on the MNIST dataset. It lists ecosystem components: TensorFlow.js for browser and Node.js use, LiteRT for mobile and edge devices (Android, iOS, Raspberry Pi, Edge TPU), tf.data for input pipelines, TFX for production MLOps pipelines, tf.keras for high-level model building, Kaggle Models, TensorFlow Datasets, and TensorBoard for visualization and tracking. It also points to community interest groups and learning resources.
notable: Ecosystem spanning training, browser (TensorFlow.js), mobile/edge (LiteRT), and production pipelines (TFX)
TensorBoard for visualizing and tracking model development
Curated curriculums and learning resources for beginners
caveats: Page does not state a license explicitly; open-source status comes from the listing description
